   - Build dynamic routes for UID-based documents.

6. **Add shared presentation**

   - Test accessibility, keyboard navigation, responsive layouts, metadata, and broken links.

    - Deploy to the chosen Next.js-compatible host.
    - Configure production environment variables, Prismic webhooks, redirects, monitoring, and analytics.

2. Scaffold Next.js

   - Create a TypeScript Next.js project using the App Router.
   - Add linting, formatting, styling, environment-variable templates, and path aliases.
   - Establish the root layout, global styles, fonts, header, footer, and error/not-found pages.

3. Connect Prismic

   - Run `npx prismic init --repo <repository>` to install packages and generate the client, configuration, preview routes, slice simulator, and revalidation endpoint.
   - Configure route resolvers and any private-repository access token.
   - Commit generated models and TypeScript definitions.

4. Model the content

   - Give pages stable UIDs, SEO fields, social images, and a Slice Zone.
   - Document field constraints so editors know image sizes, character limits, and required content.

5. Build the slice system

   - Implement each reusable section as a typed slice component.
   - Support deliberate variations instead of one oversized, heavily conditional slice.
   - Create representative mock content and test slices through the simulator.
   - Ensure responsive behavior, semantic markup, keyboard access, and optimized Prismic images.

6. Implement routing and rendering

   - Fetch Prismic data directly in async Server Components.
   - Build homepage and dynamic UID routes.
   - Add route resolution for every document type and locale.
   - Implement `generateStaticParams` where useful and return `notFound()` for missing documents.
   - Keep client-side JavaScript limited to genuinely interactive components.

   - Configure local and production preview URLs.
   - Register a publishing webhook against `/api/revalidate` so changes update without a full rebuild.
   - Test drafts, published edits, unpublishing, and broken-link behavior.

8. Complete SEO and discovery

   - Generate per-page metadata from Prismic SEO fields.
   - Add canonical URLs, Open Graph data, robots rules, and a dynamic sitemap.
   - Include structured data where relevant.
   - Use Next.js metadata file conventions for icons and social assets.  
   [Next.js metadata documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images)

9. Validate quality

   - Unit-test shared transformations and route helpers.
   - Add component tests for important slices and end-to-end tests for core journeys.
   - Check accessibility, responsive layouts, empty/long content, preview mode, and 404s.
   - Run linting, type checking, production builds, Lighthouse, and link validation in CI.

10. Deploy and hand off

   - Deploy to Vercel or another supported Next.js host.
   - Configure repository name, access tokens, site URL, preview URLs, and revalidation webhook.
   - Add a staging environment before production.
   - Provide an editor guide covering page creation, slice usage, previews, releases, and image requirements.
